supporting_evidence_verified: EHR problem "Disorder of kidney due to diabetes" (2007)
Heavy proteinuria (urine protein 374.9 mg/dL, ACR 468.3 mg/g)
evidence_gaps: 24‑h urine protein or spot protein/creatinine ratio to quantify proteinuria
Longitudinal A1c trend to confirm chronic hyperglycaemia burden
Renal biopsy if proteinuria is disproportionate or atypical
concerns: Probability slightly low given classic presentation; diabetic nephropathy should dominate the differential.

supporting_evidence_verified: Age 74 and CKD Stage 4 make hypertension common
evidence_gaps: Current and historic blood pressure readings
Antihypertensive medication list
Evidence of hypertensive end‑organ damage (LVH, retinal changes)
concerns: No documented hypertension; contribution is speculative.

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Cardiorenal syndrome type 2 (chronic HF worsening CKD)
supporting_evidence_verified: Prior STEMI (2010) and prosthetic aortic valve suggest possible chronic cardiac dysfunction
evidence_gaps: Recent echocardiogram (EF, valve function)
BNP/NT‑proBNP levels
Physical exam findings of heart failure (edema, JVD, rales)
concerns: No objective cardiac data; diagnosis remains conjectural.

evidence_gaps: Current antiplatelet/anticoagulation status
Recent coronary imaging or stress test

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Primary glomerular disease (membranous, FSGS, amyloidosis, etc.)
supporting_evidence_verified: Nephrotic‑range proteinuria (urine protein 374.9 mg/dL, ACR 468.3 mg/g) which is higher than typical for pure diabetic nephropathy at this stage
evidence_gaps: 24‑h urine protein quantification
Serologies (anti‑PLA2R, ANA, complement levels)
Renal imaging and possible biopsy if proteinuria >3 g/day or atypical features
concerns: Probability may be understated given the disproportionate proteinuria.

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Medication‑induced or contrast‑related acute‑on‑chronic kidney injury
evidence_gaps: Full medication reconciliation (NSAIDs, ACE‑I/ARB, diuretics, SGLT2‑i, nephrotoxins)
Recent exposure to iodinated contrast or other nephrotoxic agents
concerns: No documented exposure; probability likely over‑estimated.

supporting_evidence_verified: Advanced age and atherosclerotic burden raise theoretical risk
evidence_gaps: Renal ultrasound with Doppler
CT/MR angiography of renal arteries
Symptoms of obstruction (flank pain, sudden creatinine rise)
concerns: No imaging or clinical clues; low likelihood.

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Anemia of chronic kidney disease (mixed with possible iron deficiency)
evidence_gaps: Iron studies (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation)
Vitamin B12/folate if indicated

supporting_evidence_verified: Documented intimate‑partner abuse, low socioeconomic status, unemployment, criminal record
evidence_gaps: PHQ‑9 or GAD‑7 screening results
Psychiatric evaluation notes, antidepressant prescriptions
concerns: Psychosocial burden likely impacts adherence; screening is needed.

consistency_checks.detail: All severity ≥3 labs (eGFR, proteinuria, ACR, creatinine, LDL‑C, total cholesterol, hemoglobin) are linked to at least one diagnosis in the differential.
Blood pressure values and current medication list are absent, limiting verification of hypertensive nephrosclerosis, medication‑induced AKI, and cardio‑renal assessment.

top_concerns: Absence of blood pressure measurements and antihypertensive medication data.
No quantified proteinuria (24‑h or spot protein/creatinine) to guide need for renal biopsy.
Lack of recent cardiac evaluation (echocardiogram, BNP) to confirm or refute cardiorenal syndrome.
Missing iron studies to fully characterize anemia of CKD.
Unaddressed psychosocial screening for depression and safety planning.
review_summary: The junior differential captures the major organ systems and correctly prioritises diabetic nephropathy, but probabilities for several items are mis‑scaled and key data (BP, meds, protein quantification, cardiac imaging, iron studies, mental‑health screening) are missing. Adjusted probabilities reflect the strength of evidence, and additional comorbidities (CKD‑MBD, HFpEF, adherence issues) should be incorporated into the care plan.
